intro: When you search for construction insurance near me, you likely need cover for a building project, your tools and plant, or the liability that comes with employing others on site. A local insurance broker can help you find the right policies for your trade or project. iComply introduces you to a UK insurance broker who will quote you directly, with prices on application.
need_heading: What people searching for construction insurance near me usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for construction insurance near me need a broker who understands the risks of building work and can arrange cover that fits their contract.
needs: You are a builder or tradesperson starting a new project and need contract works cover to protect the work in progress.
You employ or subcontract people on site and need employers' liability cover, which is a legal requirement for most employers.
You hire plant or equipment for a job and need cover for that hired machinery while it is on site.
A client or main contractor has asked to see proof of public liability insurance before you can start work.
You need to insure your own tools and equipment against theft or damage while you are working on a construction site.
context_heading: Understanding construction insurance and how brokers work
context: Construction insurance is not a single product; it can include public liability, employers' liability, contract works and plant cover. A broker will assess your demands and needs, explain the key features and exclusions of each policy, and tell you how they are paid. They must be authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) or be an appointed representative of an authorised firm, so you can check them on the FCA register.

Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association (BIBA), and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute. If you have a complaint that is not resolved, you can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. When comparing quotes, look at the limits of cover, the excesses, and whether the policy meets the requirements of your contract.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the type of construction work you do, such as general building, roofing, groundworks or specialist trades.
Explain whether you need cover for a specific project or ongoing business cover.
State whether you employ anyone or use subcontractors, as this affects employers' liability requirements.
Mention any plant or equipment you hire or own that needs cover.
Give the approximate value of the works or the contract value, if you know it.
Say whether a client or contract requires specific insurance limits or types of cover.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the insurance broker
questions: What limits of cover will my contract require, and how do I check that?
Does contract works cover include materials on site and off site?
Is hired plant covered, and are there any restrictions on where it can be used?
What exclusions apply to my type of construction work?
How will you be paid for arranging my policy?
What should I do if I need to make a claim?

faqs.q: Do I need employers' liability insurance for construction work?
faqs.a: Most employers in the UK are required by law to have employers' liability insurance. If you employ anyone, even family members, you should check whether you need it. A broker can confirm the rules for your situation.

Contract works insurance covers the building project itself while it is under construction, including materials and work in progress. It can protect against damage or loss during the project. A broker can explain how it fits with your other cover.

faqs.q: Can I get cover for hired plant and equipment?
faqs.a: Yes, hired plant can be covered under a construction insurance policy. You should tell the broker what plant you hire and how it will be used. They will explain any conditions or exclusions.

faqs.q: How do I check that an insurance broker is authorised?
faqs.a: You can check whether a broker is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) on the FCA register. Many brokers also belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association (BIBA).

extra_heading: What 'near me' means for construction insurance
extra: Searching for construction insurance near me suggests you want a broker who understands local building conditions and can meet you face to face if needed. A nearby broker may have experience with the types of projects common in your area, from domestic extensions to commercial fit-outs, and can explain how local factors such as flood risk or listed building rules affect your cover. They can also visit your site or premises to assess the risks first-hand, which can help when arranging contract works or plant cover.

When you contact a broker, they will typically ask about your trade, the work you do, and any specific contract requirements. They may also want to know about your turnover, employees, and the plant or equipment you use. This helps them understand your demands and needs and find suitable policies. You can ask whether they have experience with construction insurance and whether they are authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

Comparing brokers is not about finding the cheapest; it is about finding one who explains things clearly and offers cover that matches your contract. Ask each broker what limits they recommend, what exclusions apply, and how they are paid. A good broker will welcome these questions and help you understand the trade-offs.

extra_faqs.q: How do I choose a construction insurance broker near me?
extra_faqs.a: Look for a broker who is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and has experience with construction risks. Ask how they will assess your needs and explain your options, and check that they can meet the requirements of your contract.

extra_faqs.q: Can a local broker help with contract works and plant cover?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, a local broker can arrange contract works cover to protect your project and plant cover for hired equipment. They will explain any conditions, such as where plant can be used, and help you meet your contractual obligations.
